slides.title: Safe access that emits fixed Luau
slides.thesis: Eight operators cover the nil checks that Roblox code writes by hand. Each one has a fixed emit. The compiler never looks at a type.
slides.src:
local hp = player?.Character?.Humanoid?.Health ?? 100
local spawn = workspace->Map->Spawns->Spawn1
local gui = player.PlayerGui=>Hud=>Health
cache[key] ??= compute(key)
local root = model.PrimaryPart!
slides.emit:
local _1 = (if player == nil then nil else player.Character) local _2 = (if _1 == nil then nil else _1.Humanoid) local _3 = (if _2 == nil then nil else _2.Health) local hp = (if _3 == nil then 100 else _3)
_1 = (if workspace == nil then nil else workspace:FindFirstChild("Map")) _2 = (if _1 == nil then nil else _1:FindFirstChild("Spawns")) local spawn = (if _2 == nil then nil else _2:FindFirstChild("Spawn1"))
local gui = player.PlayerGui:WaitForChild("Hud"):WaitForChild("Health")
if cache[key] == nil then cache[key] = compute(key) end
local root = (if model.PrimaryPart == nil then error("model.PrimaryPart is nil") else model.PrimaryPart)
points: ?. ?: ?[ ?( guard one link; one ? guards every later link in the chain.
?? tests nil only, so false survives. ??= assigns once, and an index on the left runs once.
-> is FindFirstChild and => is WaitForChild. A name with spaces is a string, a dynamic one goes in brackets.
! asserts not nil and quotes the source text in its message. It is only ever that, so a!(b) needs no parentheses.

slides.title: Imports are sugar over require
slides.thesis: Paths pass through unchanged. A Luau alias, a relative path, or a package works the way it already does. Type-only imports cost nothing at runtime.
slides.src:
import { add, type Item } from "./inventory"
import * as React from "@packages/react"
export const MAX = 64
points: Every form: { a, b as c, type T }, * as M, a default name, and import type.
Exports gather into the table the module returns at the end of its scope; export default returns one value.
Completion inside the braces lists the target module's exports, and a missing name offers an auto-import.
.aly, .alx, and .luau require each other freely, since all of them compile to .luau.

slides.title: async functions return a Future
slides.thesis: The body runs on task.spawn under xpcall, and the Future memoizes the result. await yields until it settles. try await turns a failure into a Result.
slides.src:
async function load(id: number): Profile
    local raw = store:GetAsync(`p/{id}`)
    return decode(raw)
end
local profile = await load(1)
local safe = try await load(2)
slides.emit:
local __alloy = require("@alloy") function load(id: number): __alloy.Future<Profile> return __alloy.future(function()
    local raw = store:GetAsync(`p/{id}`)
    return decode(raw)
end) end
local profile = __alloy.await(load(1))
local _1 = __alloy.try_await(load(2)) if _1.tag == "Err" then return _1 end local safe = _1._1
points: The declared type is the inner one. async function f(): number is a Future<number> to callers; a missing type is inferred, and the hint offers the inner type.
async do ... end gives a Future from a block, Future.all, race, any, and all_settled combine them.
Hover shows Future<T>, never the runtime's table shape.

slides.title: Enums carry payloads; match compiles to an if-chain
slides.thesis: A payload enum is a tagged table with a constructor per variant and a union type the analyzer can narrow. A unit enum is a string literal union, so it serializes for free.
slides.src:
enum Msg as
    Join(Player)
    Chat(Player, string)
end
local who = match msg with
    case Join(p) then p.Name
    case Chat(p, text) then `{p.Name}: {text}`
end
slides.emit:
local Msg = {} Msg.__index = Msg
    function Msg.Join(_1) return setmetatable({ tag = "Join", _1 = _1 }, Msg) end
    function Msg.Chat(_1, _2) return setmetatable({ tag = "Chat", _1 = _1, _2 = _2 }, Msg) end
function Msg.is(v) return (type(v) == "table" and getmetatable(v) == Msg) end type Msg = { tag: "Join", _1: Player } | { tag: "Chat", _1: Player, _2: string }
local who = (
    if type(msg) == "table" and msg.tag == "Join" then msg._1.Name
    else `{msg._1.Name}: {msg._2}`
)
points: Patterns nest: or-patterns, struct patterns, table and array patterns, literals, guards with where, and default.
match is a statement or an expression; the expression form parenthesizes so it drops into any position.
impl Msg adds methods to an enum the way it does to a struct.
Hover on a variant shows Msg.Chat(Player, string) even inside a pattern, where the emit has only a string.

slides.title: Bindings in conditions, narrowed where they live
slides.thesis: if local, elseif local, while local, and the expression form bind a value and test it in one step. The branch declares the name from the tested temp. Inside the branch it is T, not T?, and closures see the same.
slides.src:
if local player = first_player() then
    print(player.Name)
end
while local job = table.remove(queue) do
    run(job)
end
slides.emit:
do local _c1 = first_player() if _c1 then local player = _c1
    print(player.Name)
end end
while true do local _c1 = table.remove(queue) if not (_c1) then break end local job = _c1
    run(job)
end
points: where adds a filter: if local p = f() where p.AccountAge > 30 then.
Several bindings chain: if local p = a; local c = p.Character then runs the second only when the first is truthy.
Pattern forms bind too: if local Ok(v) = result then, while local Move(target) = next() do.
if not local x = f() then return end is the guard clause; x stays in scope after it.

slides.title: Structs, traits, and impls emit the metatable pattern
slides.thesis: An Alloy struct is a plain table that vanilla Luau can use. Fields carry defaults and read or write marks. impl adds methods. A trait is a type of signatures plus default bodies.
slides.src:
struct Vec2 as
    x: number
    y: number = 0
end
impl Vec2
    function len(self): number
        return math.sqrt(self.x ^ 2 + self.y ^ 2)
    end
end
local v = new Vec2 { x = 3, y = 4 }
slides.emit:
local Vec2 = {} Vec2.__index = Vec2 setmetatable(Vec2, { __call = function(_, f) if f.y == nil then f.y = 0 end return setmetatable(f, Vec2) end }) function Vec2.new(f) return Vec2(f) end


 type Vec2 = typeof(setmetatable({} :: { x: number, y: number? }, Vec2))
do
    function Vec2.len(self): number
        return math.sqrt(self.x ^ 2 + self.y ^ 2)
    end
end
local v = Vec2({ x = 3, y = 4 })
points: new is the only way in. new Vec2 { ... } is the fields form; a struct whose impl writes new or New takes new Vec2(...) instead. Bare Vec2 { } and Vec2(1, 2) are diagnostics.
@derive(Eq, Debug, Clone, Serialize) is pure codegen from the field list.
Operator traits map to metamethods: impl Add for Vec2 puts __add on the instance metatable.
Generic bounds <T: Shape> become (T & Shape) on each parameter.

slides.title: Interfaces, mapped types, and type functions
slides.thesis: interface is sugar over type with extends. Partial, Readonly, and Sink are language-level types. Type functions that the real solver runs build them, and a file may replace any of them with its own.
slides.src:
interface Entity extends Named, Positioned as
    read id: number
    write sink: (string) -> ()
end
local function patch(e: Entity, changes: Partial<Entity>): Entity
    return { ...e, ...changes }
end
points: T[], read T[], write T[] name Array<T>, ReadArray<T>, and WriteArray<T>.
{ [K in keyof T]: T[K]? } and its read and write forms compile to generated type functions.
type function Keys(t) works as in Luau, and hovers as type function Keys.
Hover keeps your annotation, changes: Partial<Entity>, instead of the analyzer's expansion.

slides.title: Shapes Luau rejects today, each with a one-line emit
slides.thesis: A ternary, an object initializer, array destructuring, a method reference, and delete with runtime dispatch. Every form keeps its line.
slides.src:
local tier = level > 5 ? "high" : "low"
local part = new Instance("Part") {
    Name = "Marker",
    Anchored = true,
}
local [ head, ...rest ] = [ 1, 2, 3 ]
button.Activated:Connect(self:on_click)
delete part
slides.emit:
local __alloy = require("@alloy") local tier = (if level > 5 then "high" else "low")
local part = Instance.new("Part")
    part.Name = "Marker"
    part.Anchored = true

local _1 = __alloy.Array.from({ 1, 2, 3 }) local head, rest = _1[1], __alloy.Array.slice(_1, 2)
button.Activated:Connect(__alloy.bind(self, self.on_click))
__alloy.delete(part)
points: c ? a : b nests, and a fused x:upper() inside a branch stays a method call.
The initializer assigns one field per line, so a field that throws traces to its own line, and the binding hovers with its class.
delete picks Disconnect, disconnect, Destroy, or destroy at runtime, so a user class and a signal both work.
const passes through to Luau's own, so a reassignment is a compile error; x in t, ...spread, bnot and the other word operators, and interpolated strings with Alloy in the holes.

slides.title: Extension methods on foreign types
slides.thesis: impl Vector3 or impl string adds methods to a type you do not own. The server injects each method into the analyzer's definitions. The call types, completes, and hovers like a built-in.
slides.src:
export impl Vector3
    function flat(self): Vector3
        return Vector3.new(self.X, 0, self.Z)
    end
end
local f = pos:flat()
slides.emit:
local __alloy = require("@alloy") do local __impl = __alloy.impl_for("Vector3")
    function __impl.flat(self): Vector3
        return Vector3.new(self.X, 0, self.Z)
    end
end
local f = __alloy.call(pos, "flat")
points: Project wide. The build and the server collect every extension first, so a call from another file dispatches too.
Primitives such as string go through a typed helper table, since a definitions file cannot add a method to string values.
The check artifact keeps pos:flat() as written and types self; the ship artifact routes through the dispatcher, which prefers the receiver's own method.

slides.title: Intrinsics and macros with a $ sigil
slides.thesis: Intrinsics see source text and position. A macro is a compile-time template with expression parameters. Its declaration leaves blank lines, and each call expands in place.
slides.src:
macro clamp01(x)
    math.clamp(x, 0, 1)
end
local ratio = $clamp01(speed / 16)
$assert_eq(ratio, 1)
local field = $nameof(RunService.Heartbeat)
slides.emit:
local __alloy = require("@alloy")


local ratio = math . clamp ( (speed / 16) , 0 , 1 )
__alloy.assert_eq("macros.aly:5", "ratio", ratio, "1", 1)
local field = "Heartbeat"
points: The set is closed: $dbg, $todo, $unreachable, $assert, $assert_eq, $nameof, $stringify, $matches, $bnot.
A macro body sees globals and its parameters, never a module local, since it expands in the calling file.
$ opens completion with every intrinsic and every macro in the workspace; a macro hovers with its header.

slides.title: Attributes with checked placement
slides.thesis: Built-in attributes drive codegen. Declared ones are metadata with typed arguments, and Attributes reads them at runtime. Completion after @ lists only what fits the position.
slides.emit:
local Item = {} Item.__index = Item setmetatable(Item, { __call = function(_, f)  return setmetatable(f, Item) end }) function Item.new(f) return Item(f) end



 type Item = typeof(setmetatable({} :: { count: number }, Item)) __alloy.attrs(Item, { own = { icon = { "rbxassetid://100" } }, fields = { count = { range = { 0, 99 } } } })
points: Placement is checked: a wire width on a plain function parameter, or any attribute on a local, is a diagnostic and leaves the emit.
@test marks an inline test; @native, @checked, @deprecated, @inline, @noinline pass through to Luau.
Hover shows @icon(asset: string) and what it goes on, the same shape as the built-in ones.

slides.title: Typed remotes with generated serializers
slides.thesis: One declaration names the parameters, their wire widths, and the side that fires. The compiler generates the serializer. fire, fire_all, on, and call are the whole surface.
slides.src:
export remote Damage(target: Player, @u16 amount: number) from client
export remote Toast(message: string, seconds: number = 3) from server
export remote function GetProfile(id: number) -> Profile from client

Damage.on(function(player, target, amount) end)
local profile = await GetProfile.call(1)
slides.emit:
local __alloy = require("@alloy") local Damage = __alloy.remote({ name = "Damage", from = "client", params = { { "target", "Player" }, { "amount", "number", u16 = {} } } })
local Toast = __alloy.remote({ name = "Toast", from = "server", params = { { "message", "string" }, { "seconds", "number", default = 3 } } })
local GetProfile = __alloy.remote({ name = "GetProfile", from = "client", params = { { "id", "number" } }, returns = "Profile" })

Damage.on(function(player, target, amount) end)
local profile = __alloy.await(GetProfile.call(1))
points: from client, from server, from client or server; completion offers the sides in that order, and only there.
@unreliable, @ratelimit, @timeout, @immediate, @validate shape one remote each.
@u8 to @f32 set a number's wire width, on a remote parameter or a struct field.

slides.title: ALX: markup that lowers to your UI library
slides.thesis: An .alx file is luaux markup with Alloy inside the holes. Tags, attributes, fragments, and comments lower to the configured factory. The language server answers hover and completion for tags and attributes itself.
points: {if ... then <Tag/> else nil} and {match ...} work inside a hole, since Alloy syntax does.
<> ... </> is a fragment; <!-- --> is a comment between tags.
The grammar colors an element from its head to its matching closing tag, and the semantic tokens of the lowered code stay out of the way.

slides.title: Inline tests that vanish from the ship artifact
slides.thesis: A @test function runs under alloy test. The ship artifact blanks it line for line. The check artifact keeps it typed, so the editor still sees it.
points: Line for line: the four source lines become four blank lines, so every later line keeps its number.
The std has its own suite: ten lest specs, sixty tests, over Result, Future, Array, HashMap, Set, Symbol, Signal, dispatch, Attributes, and the helpers.

stdItems: Array
Literals with the shared metatable: map, filter, find, reduce, slice, concat, sort_by, join.
HashMap
get, set, has, remove, keys, values, entries, get_or_insert, clear.
Set
add, has, remove, union, intersection, difference, to_array.
Queue
push, pop, peek, len; a for loop reads it front to back.
Heap
push, pop, peek under a comparator; to_array sorts.
Scope
add, remove, clean, extend; a cleanup bag that delete drains.
Iter
from, range, map, filter, take, skip, chain, collect, reduce.
Result
Ok and Err with unwrap, expect, unwrap_or, map, map_err; try and ? for early returns.
Future
future, resolve, reject, delay, all, race, any, all_settled, cancel, andThen.
Signal
The RBXScriptSignal shape: Connect, Once, Wait, Fire, FireDeferred; wrap and collect for any signal-like source.
Symbol
A unique key no string can collide with.
Attributes
get, field, variant, of, fields: the metadata attributes declared.
Partial, Readonly, Sink
Mapped types built by type functions, overridable per file.
